sn35.28:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Gaya, at Gaya’s Head, together with a thousand bhikkhus.
sn35.28:1.2: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn35.28:1.4: And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is burning?
sn35.28:1.5: The eye is burning, forms are burning, eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning.
sn35.28:1.7: Burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, I say.
sn35.28:1.11: The mind is burning … and whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning.
sn35.28:1.13: Burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, I say.
sn35.28:1.14: “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye, towards forms, towards eye-consciousness, towards eye-contact, towards whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—
sn35.28:1.15: whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant; experiences revulsion towards the ear … towards the mind … towards whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition….
sn35.28:1.16: Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.28:1.17: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
sn35.28:2.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn35.28:2.2: Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
sn35.28:2.3: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the thousand bhikkhus were liberated from the taints by nonclinging.
